text:
Sara (PM): heads up — I'm trying to land a lightweight rubric for how we pick and prioritize design partners next quarter. want something that balances strategic impact with bandwidth.
Mike (Eng): +1. can we keep it simple? ops can't handle too many high-touch partners at once.
Jamie (ProdOps): we should weight how likely they are to complete weekly feedback cycles. response rate is a hard constraint.
Ana (Research): agree. also capture signal quality — demos + recorded sessions beat single surveys for product insights.
Taylor (Design): diversity of use-cases matters. want at least 3 industry verticals and 2 small teams (<10 engineers) per wave.
Sara (PM): sketch of signals i'm thinking: engagement (30%), expected revenue/strategic-opportunity (25%), domain-fit (20%), feedback quality (15%), data-sensitivity/risk (10%). open to swapping weights.
Mike (Eng): ops-wise risk should reduce weight, not kill candidates. maybe treat high data-sensitivity as needing private deployment path rather than immediate exclusion.
Ana (Research): proposal for a quick scoring formula we can compute in a spreadsheet:
```
score = 0.3*engage + 0.25*revenue + 0.2*domain_fit + 0.15*feedback_quality + 0.1*(1 - data_sensitivity)
```
Taylor (Design): that formula makes sense. can we add a soft flag for 'must-have integrations' (e.g., vector DBs) so we can prioritize partners who help unblock infra?
Sara (PM): yes — add a boolean tag we use to nudge candidates up in tie-breaks. call it "integration-leverage".
Jamie (ProdOps): operational constraints: max 8 active DP slots per sprint, 4 of which can be high-touch. recommend we run in waves and reserve 2 slots for fast follow-ups.
Mike (Eng): +1. also note: we need to capture expected sequence lengths and latency SLO needs from partners — that affects model variant recommendations. include as a metadata field in intake form.
Ana (Research): sample intake questions: "How often will your team run evals?", "Expected prompt length and session concurrency", "Primary success metric (latency/cost/accuracy)". keep most answers multiple choice for scoring.
Taylor (Design): timeline request: recruit wave 1 by end of month, run 6-week feedback loop, decision gates at week 3 and week 6.
Sara (PM): proposed launch/readiness criteria for a DP -> beta promotion: consistent feedback cadence (>=75% weeks), no blocking infra gaps, measurable improvement on 1 signal (e.g., reduced latency or improved passage accuracy).
Jamie (ProdOps): i'll add these as acceptance checks in the intake sheet and set up automated reminders via product-bot.
product-bot: reminder set — will ping participants 48h before week 3 and week 6 reviews. :robot_face:
Sara (PM): action items: Jamie to update intake form + automations, Ana to draft scoring sheet, Taylor to map diversity targets, Mike to add infra metadata fields. i'll consolidate and post a short playbook tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Mike (Eng): ack.
Ana (Research): can do.
Taylor (Design): on it.
Jamie (ProdOps): will update the sheet and share a link in #product when done.
Sara (PM): thanks all — aiming for a recruiting shortlist by next Tue.
